text:
nora: Quick idea: extract prompt transforms into a tiny sandboxed sidecar that runs tenant rules as WASM modules. Main goals: unstick runtime hotpath, let product owners ship rules faster, and improve security isolation.

diego: I like it. Two deployment modes: colocated unix-socket sidecar for low-latency Dedicated customers, and a shared HTTP pool for Hosted.

linda: Security notes: modules must be signed and come from an immutable registry. No outbound networking from modules; logging via host-provided handle.

nora: Interface sketch: minimal RPC -> {tenant_id, raw_prompt, profile_hint} -> {transformed_prompt, transform_version, patches}. gRPC primary, JSON fallback.

diego: Perf concern: added hop could affect p99. Targets: local socket p50 <1ms, p99 <4ms; shared pool p50 <2ms, p99 <9ms. Plan to measure per-module overhead.

linda: Rollout: mirror-canary new module for a small percent of traffic, compute transform_diff_pct. Auto-revert if diff > 0.2% or p99 latency regresses > 20%.

infra-bot: Helm chart stub created, metrics: preprocess_latency_ms, transform_diff_pct, module_crash_count, module_cache_hit_rate. Runbook link: /runbook/preproc-wasm-extract.

nora: I'll draft RFC with API, signing/registry, canary thresholds, and fallback semantics (last-good module + runtime-native transforms). Posting draft tomorrow for reviews.
